one_liner: Rust Bloom filter crate: classic non-blocked layout, faster lookups than other Rust Bloom crates, plus a lock-free atomic variant.
what_it_does: A standard approximate-membership Bloom filter: no false negatives, no deletes, fixed memory once built. You size it with a builder, either with_num_bits(n) or with_false_pos(p), then finish with expected_items(k), hashes(k) or items(iter). insert and contains take any &impl Hash, and there are raw-hash entry points (source_hash, insert_hash, contains_hash) for pre-hashed keys. AtomicBloomFilter has the same API with every method on &self, so it replaces RwLock<BloomFilter> for shared use, and both types support union, intersect, clear and optional serde.
how_it_is_fast: Each item is hashed once, to 64 bits. The other k-1 bit positions come from cheap double hashing (Kirsch-Mitzenmacher, 'Less hashing, same performance'): h2 = h1 * constant, then each next index is rotl(h1, 5) + h2, instead of k separate hash calls. Indexes are mapped to the bit array with Lemire's multiply-shift fast range reduction rather than modulo. contains returns on the first unset bit, so a non-member usually costs one hash and one or two memory probes. The bit array is a plain boxed u64 slice with no SIMD and no blocking; since 0.17 the author deliberately chose a non-blocked layout, trading member-check speed for accuracy and faster non-member rejection (issue #20).
when_to_use: Rust services where most queries are misses, such as cache or disk-read avoidance or dedup pre-checks, since non-member checks are its strongest case (1.36 ns vs 5-43 ns for other crates on the author's benchmark).
Filters that grow by incremental inserts at runtime and may need union or intersect, which a build-once xor or fuse filter cannot do.
Many threads inserting and querying one filter: AtomicBloomFilter uses fetch_or on AtomicU64 words with no lock.
Low false-positive targets per bit: the author's accuracy chart shows it tracking the classic-Bloom curve, well below the blocked sbbf and below bloom and bloomfilter at the same load.
no_std or embedded targets with alloc: CI checks thumbv7em-none-eabi, and portable-atomic covers targets without native 64-bit atomics.
when_not_to_use: Workloads dominated by positive lookups: a member check touches k random words, and on the author's own chart the SIMD split-block sbbf is faster (5.30 ns vs 7.67 ns).
Filters much larger than cache: non-blocked probes each risk a cache miss. The published numbers come only from a 64 KiB, cache-resident filter, and DRAM-scale behaviour is not measured.
Static key sets built once: a xor or binary fuse filter (xorf) gives smaller filters and constant-probe lookups.
Needs deletion or counting: not supported. A counting Bloom filter (issue #10) and xor filters (issue #7) are open requests.
Cross-language or cross-version persisted filters: no C API, and 0.17 changed the algorithm, so serialized filters are incompatible with earlier versions.

integration.dependencies: foldhash, siphasher, libm, portable-atomic (always); rand (default feature), serde and loom (optional features)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.70 (rust-version in Cargo.toml; CI has an MSRV job on 1.70), edition 2021
integration.platforms: any Rust target, with no arch-specific or SIMD code; std and no_std+alloc, with thumbv7em-none-eabi checked in CI; tests run on ubuntu-latest
integration.thread_safety: BloomFilter needs &mut self to insert (wrap it in RwLock to share). AtomicBloomFilter is lock-free: all methods take &self and use Relaxed atomics, so there is no ordering guarantee between one thread's insert and another's contains without external synchronization.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same semantics as a classic Bloom filter (no false negatives, no deletes), but it has its own builder API, and its bit layout and serde format do not interoperate with other crates or with fastbloom before 0.17

gotchas: The default hasher is SipHash-1-3 with a random key per filter. Filters built separately cannot be unioned, intersected or compared unless both use .seed(&u128) or the same hasher, and union and intersect do not check this. Note also that the headline benchmark swapped in foldhash.

Every probe is derived from one 64-bit hash, so a weak custom hasher (or raw values fed to insert_hash) degrades all k positions at once. The README says hashes are built from 32-bit halves, but the 0.17 code actually multiplies and rotates a single 64-bit hash.

k comes from ln2 * bits / items, and the minimum size is 64 bits, so tiny expected_items gives huge k (issue #17: 354 hashes for 1 item when the minimum was 512 bits; expected_items(0) meant u32::MAX hashes before the clamp to 1). In 0.15-0.16, hashes(0) panicked; 0.17 clamps it to 1.

Recent correctness fixes, so pin to 0.17 or later: AtomicBitVec::set returned the wrong value until 0.14.1, and filters above u32::MAX bits (about 512 MiB) mapped every index into a u32 range, causing mass false positives, until 0.16 (issue #22). The src/ tree has no unsafe code.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over xorf when you need incremental or concurrent inserts rather than a build-once static set. Pick it over the Impala-style SIMD blocked Bloom (efficient/cuckoofilter) or a cuckoo filter when you are in Rust, misses dominate and you want classic-Bloom accuracy per bit without deletes. Choose a blocked Bloom when hits dominate or the filter lives in DRAM, and a cuckoo filter when you need deletion.
verified_claims_summary: The author's Criterion microbenchmark on an AMD Ryzen 9 5900X measures per-lookup latency for u64 keys in a 64 KiB filter holding 45,000 items (about 8 hashes each). Each iteration repeats the same 10 query keys, the rustc version and flags are unstated, and perf.py reads Windows-style paths, suggesting a Windows build. fastbloom (with foldhash) took 1.36 ns per non-member check vs 5.16 ns for sbbf (xxh3) and 14.5-42.6 ns for SipHash-based crates, and 7.67 ns per member check vs 5.30 ns for sbbf and 27-122 ns for the rest. Insert throughput, multi-threaded runs and out-of-cache filters were not measured.
status_note: Actively maintained (0.17.0 on 2026-03-01, maintainer still replying to issues in July 2026), MIT OR Apache-2.0, a small pure-safe-Rust crate with heavy real-world use (about 23.6M crates.io downloads, a dependency of quinn-proto, turso_core and libafl), but still 0.x with breaking releases every few months.
